collection.title: Exodus and wilderness
collection.scope: Twenty-five selected readings from Exodus 1 to Deuteronomy 34, ending with Moses in Moab. This is not all of the Pentateuch, a full plague sequence or every camp in Numbers 33.
collection.method: The Bible is the primary text. Short original summaries follow selected passages in reading order. Supporting publications are linked for the specific questions they address; archaeological sites, religious traditions and interpretation remain separately labelled.
collection.review: AI-assisted editorial reading aid. Selected primary chapter views and supporting source sections were checked on 28 October 2026. Independent historical, textual and archaeological specialist review remains pending.
collection.geography: The fifteen setting records include regions and grouped places. Coordinates and travel routes are deliberately unassigned; the complete stage list is the geography study interface.
collection.chronology: Reading order is not a calendar chronology. The two dated proposals appear only in the comparison panel, not as dates attached to events.

places.name: Egypt
places.note: A broad national setting. The selected passages do not identify a palace or every labour site.

places.name: The Nile in Egypt
places.note: The birth account names the Nile. No particular riverbank, palace or modern channel is identified here.

places.name: Midian
places.note: A regional setting in the Moses narrative. A named well or exact household location is not established by the selected passage.

places.name: Horeb / Sinai
places.note: Exodus 3 names Horeb; Exodus 19 names Sinai. This shared study setting links their traditional association without assigning a modern summit.

places.name: Rameses to Succoth
places.note: The departure passage names both places. Pi-Ramesse archaeology informs the Delta context; the biblical point of departure and the identification of Succoth remain distinct questions.

places.name: Etham and the wilderness approach
places.note: Exodus 13 describes Etham at the wilderness edge. No exact campsite or modern boundary is supplied.

places.name: The sea and its approach
places.note: Pi-hahiroth, Migdol and Baal-zephon are narrative locators. A precise shoreline or crossing coordinate is not assigned.

places.name: Shur, Marah and Elim
places.note: This grouped setting follows one selected passage through three named settings. It is not one town or a plotted daily itinerary.

places.name: Wilderness of Sin
places.note: Exodus 16 places this wilderness between Elim and Sinai. It is kept distinct from the wilderness of Zin in Numbers 20.

places.name: Rephidim
places.note: The text locates the camp and the Amalek encounter at Rephidim. No rock, hill or battle site is pinned.

places.name: Kadesh and the surrounding wilderness
places.note: Numbers 13 associates Kadesh with Paran; Numbers 20 names the wilderness of Zin. Archaeological proposals and the narrative settings require separate assessment.

places.name: Mount Hor
places.note: Numbers 20 places the mountain on the edge of Edom. This collection does not identify a modern mountain or shrine.

places.name: The journey around Edom
places.note: Numbers 21 describes travel by the way of the sea to go around Edom. This is a broad narrative movement with no reconstructed track.

places.name: Plains of Moab
places.note: The camp is described across the Jordan from Jericho. A particular camp footprint or crossing is not inferred.

places.name: Mount Nebo / Pisgah
places.note: Deuteronomy names Nebo and the top of Pisgah. Its statement that the burial place was unknown is preserved; no grave coordinate is suggested.

stages.title: Israel under forced labour
stages.summary: A new king oppresses Israel with forced labour, including construction at Pithom and Raamses.
stages.caution: The passage does not name the king; no pharaoh or absolute date is assigned.

stages.title: Moses rescued from the Nile
stages.summary: Moses is placed in a basket among the reeds, found by Pharaoh's daughter and cared for by his own mother before his adoption.
stages.caution: The river setting does not identify an exact rescue site.

stages.title: Moses in Midian
stages.summary: Moses flees Pharaoh, helps the daughters of Midian's priest at a well, and settles with the family, marrying Zipporah.
stages.caution: The narrative well is not equated with a modern tourist site.

stages.title: The call at Horeb
stages.summary: While tending Jethro's flock, Moses comes to Horeb and is commissioned to bring Israel out of Egypt.
stages.caution: This is before the departure from Egypt; a repeated setting is not a second Exodus route.

stages.title: Setting out for Egypt
stages.summary: Moses receives leave from Jethro and sets out toward Egypt with his family and the staff of God.
stages.caution: This reading describes departure toward Egypt, not a measured route or an arrival at a named palace.

stages.title: The Passover instructions
stages.summary: Moses and Aaron receive instructions for the Passover, including the household meal, the blood on the doorposts and continuing remembrance.
stages.caution: The instructions are selected here; the full plague sequence is outside this bounded collection.

stages.title: Departure from Rameses
stages.summary: Pharaoh orders Israel to leave. The Israelites depart from Rameses toward Succoth, carrying unleavened dough.
stages.caution: Pi-Ramesse and Avaris are archaeological settings, not interchangeable names for every narrated event.

stages.title: The wilderness way
stages.summary: God leads the people away from the nearer Philistine road. They leave Succoth, camp at Etham and are guided by the cloud and fire.
stages.caution: The passage supplies sequence and direction without fixing a modern road alignment.

stages.title: Encamped before the sea
stages.summary: Israel camps near the named sea-approach settings. Pharaoh pursues, the people are afraid and Moses tells them to await the Lord's deliverance.
stages.caution: The ancient place names do not by themselves supply a unique modern crossing location.

stages.title: Deliverance through the sea
stages.summary: The Lord opens a way through the sea for Israel. The waters return over the pursuing Egyptians, and Israel sees the Lord's deliverance.
stages.caution: The biblical account is the primary evidence for this reading. Competing modern site proposals remain separately labelled.

stages.title: Water at Marah and Elim
stages.summary: After entering Shur, the people reach bitter water at Marah. The Lord provides through Moses, and the people later camp at Elim's springs and palms.
stages.caution: The passage groups successive settings; no exact spring or daily travel track is reconstructed.

stages.title: Provision in the wilderness of Sin
stages.summary: In the wilderness of Sin, the people complain about food. The Lord provides quail and manna and gives instructions for gathering.
stages.caution: Sin and Zin are kept distinct. Proposed natural parallels are not substituted for what the passage says.

stages.title: Water at Rephidim
stages.summary: The people lack water at Rephidim. Moses cries to the Lord, strikes the rock as instructed, and the place is named Massah and Meribah.
stages.caution: This Exodus episode is kept distinct from the Meribah account at Kadesh in Numbers 20.

stages.title: The encounter with Amalek
stages.summary: Joshua leads the fighting against Amalek while Moses, Aaron and Hur go up the hill. Aaron and Hur support Moses' hands.
stages.caution: No hill, battle line or modern territorial boundary is inferred.

stages.title: Israel before Mount Sinai
stages.summary: The people leave Rephidim and camp before the mountain. Moses receives the covenant call and brings the people's response to the Lord.
stages.caution: A named biblical mountain and a modern candidate summit are separate identifications.

stages.title: The covenant words
stages.summary: God speaks the commandments, beginning with his deliverance of Israel from Egypt and setting out obligations toward God and neighbour.
stages.caution: The reading follows the cited text; later traditions differ in how they number the commandments.

stages.title: Departure from Sinai
stages.summary: The cloud rises from the tabernacle, and Israel sets out from the wilderness of Sinai toward the wilderness of Paran.
stages.caution: This transition omits intervening episodes from the selected reading list; it is not a complete camp catalogue.

stages.title: The scouts report at Kadesh
stages.summary: The scouts return to Moses, Aaron and the congregation at Kadesh. They show the land's fruit, while Caleb and the other scouts differ about entering it.
stages.caution: The selected reading is the return and report, not a plotted reconstruction of the scouting journey.

stages.title: The wilderness judgment
stages.summary: The Lord announces judgment on the grumbling generation and a forty-year wilderness period, while Caleb and Joshua are excepted.
stages.caution: The reported duration is retained without converting this stage into an independently fixed calendar date.

stages.title: Miriam and the waters of Meribah
stages.summary: Miriam dies at Kadesh. When the community lacks water, Moses strikes the rock; Moses and Aaron are told they will not bring the assembly into the land.
stages.caution: This is the Numbers 20 account in the wilderness of Zin, distinct from Exodus 17 at Rephidim.

stages.title: Edom refuses passage
stages.summary: Moses sends messengers from Kadesh requesting passage through Edom. The request is refused, and Israel turns away.
stages.caution: The text reports refusal, not an Israelite arrival inside Edom.

stages.title: Aaron dies at Mount Hor
stages.summary: Israel travels from Kadesh to Mount Hor. Aaron's garments pass to Eleazar, Aaron dies, and the congregation mourns him.
stages.caution: The narrative mountain is not equated with a particular modern shrine.

stages.title: The bronze serpent
stages.summary: During the journey around Edom, the people complain and are bitten by serpents. Moses intercedes and makes the bronze serpent as the Lord directs.
stages.caution: This selected episode does not establish the serpent's later archaeological survival or an exact campsite.

stages.title: The camp in the plains of Moab
stages.summary: Israel camps in the plains of Moab across from Jericho. Balak fears the people and sends for Balaam.
stages.caution: Balak's messengers travel to Balaam; Israel is not described here as travelling to Balaam's home.

stages.title: Moses sees the land from Nebo
stages.summary: Moses goes up from Moab to Nebo and sees the land. He dies in Moab, and Israel mourns him; the account says his burial place was not known.
stages.caution: The collection ends before the Jordan crossing. Neither an exact grave nor a modern memorial is identified as the burial site.

comparisons.title: Rameses, Avaris and Tanis
comparisons.summary: Compare the biblical place names with independently investigated Delta settlements.

candidates.title: Qantir / Pi-Ramesse
candidates.note: The excavation project identifies the Ramesside capital at Qantir. Its connection with the biblical Rameses is a further historical interpretation.

candidates.title: Tell el-Daba / Avaris
candidates.note: The Austrian project identifies Avaris and its later relationship to southern Pi-Ramesse. It is not simply interchangeable with every biblical Rameses reference.

candidates.title: Tanis
candidates.note: Reused Ramesside monuments contributed to the former identification with Pi-Ramesse; their relocation explains the confusion.

comparisons.caution: Evidence for these cities does not identify the Exodus pharaoh or establish a departure year.

comparisons.title: Which sea-crossing setting?
comparisons.summary: Compare geographic uses of yam sup with proposed Exodus crossing settings.

candidates.title: Eastern Delta lakes
candidates.note: Beitzel discusses several eastern Delta lakes and favours Timsah; these remain competing proposals.

candidates.title: Northern Gulf of Suez
candidates.note: The essay records northern Gulf of Suez proposals and questions about ancient shorelines.

candidates.title: Gulf of Aqaba / Elat
candidates.note: 1 Kings 9:26 uses the term in an Aqaba/Elat context. Beitzel rejects an Aqaba crossing on distance grounds.

comparisons.caution: Use of a sea name elsewhere does not prove that the same crossing location is intended. No candidate receives a definitive pin or route.

comparisons.title: Horeb and the mountain of Sinai
comparisons.summary: A sacred-site tradition, a regional argument and a modern summit identification have different evidential scopes.

candidates.title: Jebel Musa / Saint Catherine area
candidates.note: UNESCO documents the sacred landscape and monastery associated with Moses. This records the tradition and heritage rather than an excavated identification of the covenant event.

candidates.title: Arabia / Midian proposals
candidates.note: Hurn surveys arguments from Midian and the term Arabia. Historical regional language cannot simply be equated with a modern national border.

comparisons.caution: The comparison is selective. The collection assigns neither a modern summit nor a measured route between Horeb, Egypt and Sinai.

comparisons.title: Kadesh: an oasis, a site and a district
comparisons.summary: The publication and the biblical setting need to be read at their own geographic and chronological scales.

candidates.title: Tell el-Qudeirat
candidates.note: The IAA report identifies the oasis site as Kadesh Barnea and describes superimposed Iron Age fortresses.

candidates.title: The wider spring district, including Ein Qadis
candidates.note: The report includes a survey of Ein el-Qudeirat and Ein Qadis. The geographic extent of the biblical setting remains a separate question from any one excavated fortress.

comparisons.caution: The linked abstract and contents were checked, not the full excavation volume. Fortress dates are not automatically dates for the wilderness narratives.

comparisons.title: Two chronological readings
comparisons.summary: The collection presents selected date proposals without assigning calendar dates to its stages.

candidates.title: Fifteenth-century calculation
candidates.note: Taking the 480-year interval with a conventional date for Solomon's fourth year produces the often cited proposal around 1446 BC.

candidates.title: Ramesside-period proposal
candidates.basis: Reading of the Raamses place name
candidates.note: Crossway also describes a thirteenth-century proposal associated with Ramesses II, around 1260 BC, while noting disagreement.

comparisons.caution: Both dates are model-dependent proposals. The place name alone does not identify Pharaoh, and the stage order does not settle the chronology.

oeaw-delta.title: Tell el-Daba / Avaris excavation project
oeaw-delta.author: Austrian Archaeological Institute, Austrian Academy of Sciences
oeaw-delta.scope: The identification and settlement history of Avaris and its relationship to Pi-Ramesse.
oeaw-delta.limitation: The excavated city provides historical context; this project page does not establish a specific Exodus event or identify its pharaoh.
oeaw-delta.access: Project page read; linked excavation literature has not received an exhaustive review.
oeaw-delta.rights: Linked source only. No publisher text, illustrations or datasets are redistributed.

qantir-project.title: Pi-Ramesse: Chronicle of a City
qantir-project.author: Qantir/Pi-Ramesse Project and Roemer- und Pelizaeus-Museum exhibition
qantir-project.scope: Archaeological identification of Qantir/Pi-Ramesse and the earlier confusion with Tanis.
qantir-project.limitation: A city identification and its Ramesside history do not by themselves fix the date of the biblical departure.
qantir-project.access: The excavation exhibition chronology was read; no third-party imagery is reproduced.
qantir-project.rights: Linked source only. No publisher text, illustrations or datasets are redistributed.

beitzel-sea.title: The Location of the Biblical Red Sea
beitzel-sea.author: Barry J. Beitzel, The Ancient Near East Today, September 2021
beitzel-sea.scope: Proposed crossing settings and geographic uses of yam sup.
beitzel-sea.limitation: An attributed scholarly assessment, not a conclusive site identification.
beitzel-sea.rights: Linked source only. No publisher text, illustrations or datasets are redistributed.

unesco-catherine.title: Saint Catherine Area
unesco-catherine.author: UNESCO World Heritage Centre
unesco-catherine.scope: The Jebel Musa / Saint Catherine religious tradition and surviving monastic heritage.
unesco-catherine.limitation: A heritage designation documents the site and its tradition; it is not an excavation-based identification of the biblical mountain.
unesco-catherine.access: Heritage description and significance statement read; no text, imagery or map is republished.
unesco-catherine.rights: Linked source only. No publisher text, illustrations or datasets are redistributed.

hurn-geography.title: Identifying and Delineating the Geographic Regions of the Israelite Migration from Egypt to Canaan Using a Hydrological Approach
hurn-geography.author: Deborah Anne Hurn, Avondale University doctoral thesis, copyright 2022
hurn-geography.scope: A research survey of proposed regions and mountains, including the Arabia proposal and its textual reasoning.
hurn-geography.limitation: A thesis and its survey do not constitute consensus or independent review of this collection. Its own hydrological reconstruction is not adopted here.
hurn-geography.access: Title, abstract and selected geography-survey sections consulted; the full thesis has not been audited.
hurn-geography.rights: Linked source only. No publisher text, illustrations or datasets are redistributed.

iaa-kadesh.title: Excavations at Kadesh Barnea (Tell el-Qudeirat) 1976-1982, Part 1: Text
iaa-kadesh.author: Rudolph Cohen and Hannah Bernick-Greenberg, Israel Antiquities Authority, 2007
iaa-kadesh.scope: Published identification of Tell el-Qudeirat and the excavated Iron Age fortresses; the contents include a survey of Ein el-Qudeirat and Ein Qadis.
iaa-kadesh.limitation: The excavated fortresses cannot simply be assigned to Moses. The catalogue abstract and contents do not settle every earlier occupation or location question.
iaa-kadesh.access: Publisher abstract and contents checked; the full excavation volume and individual chapters have not been reviewed.
iaa-kadesh.rights: Linked source only. No publisher text, illustrations or datasets are redistributed.

crossway-date.title: ESV Global Study Bible: Introduction to Exodus
crossway-date.author: Crossway
crossway-date.scope: Two chronological readings: a fifteenth-century calculation and a Ramesside-period proposal.
crossway-date.limitation: These are interpretive date proposals, not calendar dates established for the stages below. No pharaoh is assigned to an event.
crossway-date.access: Public introduction read; publisher study notes are linked and not bundled.
crossway-date.rights: Linked source only. No publisher text, illustrations or datasets are redistributed.
